question.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to $6x≡1\,(\text{mod}\,35)?$
question.worked_solution:
The scalar multiplication properties of congruences state that for $k\in Z,$ we have the following:

- $a≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n)\,⟹\,ka≡kb\,(\text{mod}\,n)$

- $a≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n)\,⟹\,ka≡kb\,(\text{mod}\,kn)$

The modulus equals $35$ in all statements, which suggests we'll need to use the first property.

Notice that the coefficient of $x$ is $6,$ and $6\cdot 6=36$ is one larger than the modulus. Therefore, we can reduce the coefficient of $x$ to unity as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}6x & ≡1\, & (\text{mod}\,35) \\ 6\cdot 6x & ≡6\cdot 1\, & (\text{mod}\,35) \\ 36x & ≡6\, & (\text{mod}\,35) \\ x+35x & ≡6\, & (\text{mod}\,35) \\ x+0x & ≡6\, & (\text{mod}\,35) \\ x & ≡6\, & (\text{mod}\,35)\end{aligned}
$$
